entries.clue: Where one could get a spare item of crockery in kitchen (7,5)

definitions.text: Where one could get a spare

blocks.note: a bowl is a piece of crockery
a galley is a ship's or aircraft's kitchen

annotation.surface: Someone raiding the kitchen cupboards for a spare plate or dish.
annotation.walkthrough: A spare in ten-pin bowling is knocking down all ten pins with two balls, so the definition is about scoring, not spare crockery.
annotation.definitionFit: A bowling alley is where you bowl, and so where a player could score a spare.

entries.clue: Power cuts elsewhere succeeded suppressing generation (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, AGE sits on top of S, holding it down

annotation.surface: A report of power cuts in another region holding back electricity generation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Generation' reads as power generation in the surface; here it is a span of time. 'Suppressing' only makes sense read downwards: AGE is placed above S.
annotation.definitionFit: Outages are interruptions of supply, such as power cuts.

entries.clue: Experts defending one carrying on what predecessors left? (8)

indicators.note: ACES stand guard around I, enclosing it
in a down clue, ACIES carries LEG on top of it

blocks.note: the on side in cricket is also called the leg side
Roman numeral one, placed inside ACES

annotation.surface: A team of experts guarding someone who continues a tradition left by those before.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' = LEG is a cricket convention: the leg side and the on side are the same half of the field.
annotation.definitionFit: Legacies are what people leave to those who follow them.

entries.clue: A, B, C, D, F or G (4)

definitions.text: A, B, C, D, F or G

blocks.note: the surface reading: a run of exam grades, with E conspicuously skipped
the setter's reading: G is no grade, so these are the musical letter names A to G, minus one

annotation.surface: A bare list of letters, perhaps exam grades.
annotation.walkthrough: The list looks like school grades, but it is the seven musical note names with one missing: everything that is NOT E, which reads as NOTE.
annotation.definitionFit: Each of A, B, C, D, F and G names a musical note.

entries.clue: Advisers against you replacing setter with new rogue (5,5)

indicators.note: N takes the place of I in the letters
the letters go astray, rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged, before the swap
the setter refers to themself as I; this I leaves
n = new, which comes in instead

annotation.surface: Someone warning that a rogue has been put in charge of setting in place of the old one.
annotation.walkthrough: Swap the I of AGAINST YOU for N, then rearrange all ten letters. Agony aunts are newspaper advice columnists.
annotation.definitionFit: Agony aunts answer readers' problems in newspapers: professional advisers.

entries.clue: Briefly served up another drink one left in can for ages (5)

definitions.text: one left in can for ages

indicators.note: cut short: REFILL loses its last letter
in a down clue, the letters are turned to read upwards

blocks.note: a refill is another drink; cut short it is REFIL

annotation.surface: A pub scene: someone quickly served another round.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' is slang for prison, so the definition is a long-term prisoner, not something left in a tin.
annotation.definitionFit: A lifer is a prisoner serving a life sentence, left in jail for ages.

entries.clue: Chay going off to meet Ted sailed in style (7)

indicators.note: CHAY's letters go off course, rearranged

annotation.surface: Chay Blyth, the British round-the-world yachtsman, setting off to meet a friend by sea.
annotation.walkthrough: Chay Blyth was a famous British long-distance sailor, which is why the name belongs in a sailing surface.
annotation.definitionFit: To yacht is to sail in a yacht, the stylish way to travel by water.

entries.clue: Greek character evidently defending loud friend in French household (7,6)

indicators.note: CLEARLY surrounds FAMI, guarding it
take the French word for friend

blocks.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

annotation.surface: A Greek visitor openly sticking up for a noisy friend in a French home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' is a letter of the alphabet, not a person, and FAMI sits inside CLEARLY, split as CLEAR and LY.
annotation.definitionFit: The term names the smallest household unit: parents and their children living together, without grandparents or cousins.

entries.clue: Forebodings I should have mentioned, harbouring ill-feeling about island (13)

indicators.note: PS shelters the rest inside it
'about' in its sense of 'around', so the ill-feeling is wrapped round the island letter

blocks.note: PS, the postscript where you add what you should have mentioned; P opens
resentment = ill-feeling, split to take I

annotation.surface: Someone confessing uneasy feelings about an island, laced with bitterness.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I should have mentioned' is what a postscript says, so it stands for PS, which wraps everything else.
annotation.definitionFit: Presentiments are feelings that something, usually bad, is about to happen: forebodings.

entries.clue: In an excited state drunk becomes irritated (7)

annotation.surface: An overexcited drunk turning tetchy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' reads as a noun, a drunkard, but works as the adjective TIGHT.
annotation.definitionFit: Uptight means tense and irritable.

entries.clue: Policeman runs past where skaters relax (7)

indicators.note: R comes after, beyond, the other piece

annotation.surface: A police officer jogging past the edge of an ice rink.
annotation.walkthrough: Skaters relax once they are OFF ICE, which runs together as OFFICE.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: every policeman holds the rank of constable or above and is addressed as 'officer'.

entries.clue: Laws of generating intelligent conclusions, principally? (5)

indicators.note: take the principal, first, letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the source of the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Logic is the set of rules for reasoning soundly to conclusions.

entries.clue: The yards formed compounds (8)

indicators.note: the letters are formed into a new word

annotation.surface: Yards joined into compounds, as enclosed farm or prison yards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Compounds' looks like enclosures in this surface; it is the chemical sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Hydrates are chemical compounds containing water.

entries.clue: Can access achieved with them spread pretension? (3-7)

indicators.note: the letters are spread about and rearranged

annotation.surface: A question about whether pretension spreads through social access.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can access' reads as 'is able to access'; the can is a tin.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: 'can' is the tin, and the gadgets are the means of getting inside one.

entries.clue: Troubled about Messi not drinking much? (10)

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed, rearranged

annotation.surface: Worry that the footballer Lionel Messi drinks too little on a night out.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole of 'about Messi' is fodder; 'about' is not a container here.
annotation.definitionFit: Abstemious means moderate, especially in eating and drinking.

entries.clue: Junk energy emitted by toothless prime minister (4)

indicators.note: TAT and E are given off by the longer word, leaving it

annotation.surface: A toothless PM spouting rubbish and hot air.
annotation.walkthrough: Anthony Eden was British prime minister in the 1950s. Take TAT and E out of EDENTATE.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Sir Anthony Eden led the UK from 1955 until the Suez crisis ended his premiership in 1957.

entries.clue: Ideal fellow (8)

blocks.note: ideal in the sense of existing only as an idea: theoretical
a fellow of a college, a university teacher

annotation.surface: Two words that seem to describe the perfect chap.
annotation.walkthrough: Read together they suggest 'the ideal fellow'; separately 'ideal' means existing only as an idea, and a fellow is a university teacher.
annotation.definitionFit: Academic means theoretical, and an academic is a fellow of a college.

entries.clue: Peak Fury docked twice by international boxing judge (4)

indicators.note: FURY has its tail cut off two times
to box something in is to shut it inside, so FU and I close round the judge's letter

blocks.note: FURY minus Y, then minus R

annotation.surface: The boxer Tyson Fury docked points twice by a judge from abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: Tyson Fury is a British heavyweight boxer, so 'boxing judge' reads naturally as a ringside official; 'boxing' is the container.
annotation.definitionFit: Fuji is Japan's highest mountain peak.

entries.clue: Joel sat near us periodically indicating fools (7)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals

annotation.surface: Joel sitting near us now and again, pointing out fools.
annotation.walkthrough: Start with the J and take every other letter to the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the licensed fool of a royal court wore motley and was called a jester.

entries.clue: Fine stroke-maker caught behind by player, not stumped (10)

indicators.note: to catch a remark is to hear it, so what follows is a sound, not a spelling
remove ST, the scorecard abbreviation for stumped

blocks.note: botty is a childish word for the behind
st = stumped on a cricket scorecard, dropped

annotation.surface: A cricket report: a batsman with fine strokes caught behind by the keeper, not stumped.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all cricket, but the stroke-maker is a painter's brush. Botty is British nursery slang for bottom.
annotation.definitionFit: Botticelli, the Renaissance painter, made fine brushstrokes.

entries.clue: Escape from capsule aka Gemini (7)

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the words that follow

blocks.note: starts at the last two letters of the first word and ends two letters into the third

annotation.surface: An escape from a space capsule, the Gemini of NASA's 1960s missions.
annotation.walkthrough: Gemini was the NASA programme before Apollo; the answer runs capsu(LE AKA GE)mini across three words.
annotation.definitionFit: Escape in its sense of seepage, as when gas escapes from a pipe.

entries.clue: Mankiest bananas emerging through error of judgement (8)

definitions.note: MISTAKEN is an adjective; 'through error of judgement' is an adverbial phrase meaning much the same

indicators.note: crazy, so the letters go mad

annotation.surface: Buying the most rotten bananas in the fruit bowl by a bad call.
annotation.walkthrough: Manky is British slang for dirty or rotten, which is why bananas fit the surface; here 'bananas' means crazy.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive: a belief held through an error of judgement is a wrong one.

entries.clue: University will support advanced random number generator later (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, U goes underneath and holds up the rest

blocks.note: a = advanced, as in A level
a die produces a random number when rolled

annotation.surface: A university promising to fund an advanced random number generator in due course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Later' is a word of farewell, as in 'see you later', not an adverb of time.
annotation.definitionFit: Adieu and 'later!' are both ways of saying goodbye.

entries.clue: He dabbles in drugs, primarily with one of The Libertines (5)

indicators.note: 'primarily' means first of all, so only the first letter of drugs is used

annotation.surface: A member of the rock band The Libertines dabbling in drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: The Libertines are a British band known for drug troubles, but here a libertine is just a rake. A drake is a male dabbling duck.
annotation.definitionFit: A drake is a male duck, and ducks such as mallards dabble for food.

entries.clue: Just food and drink we hear (4)

indicators.note: the second meaning is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: just in the sense of even-handed, not 'only'

annotation.surface: Claiming to have heard that there is simply food and drink on offer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'only' before 'food and drink'; it means fair-minded.
annotation.definitionFit: Fair means just, even-handed.

entries.clue: Flow of water sent back to correct swimmer (3,4)

indicators.note: the letters are sent back, read in reverse

annotation.surface: Water sent back to put right a swimmer's stroke.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' in crosswords is often a fish; here the eel.
annotation.definitionFit: A lee tide is a tidal flow running with the wind.

entries.clue: Predator's gun back from Saturday at around noon (4,3)

indicators.note: take the back, last, letter of Saturday
'around' in its sense of 'surrounding', so AT is placed about the N

annotation.surface: A hunter's gun being brought back on Saturday around midday.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's in 'Predator's' joins the definition to the wordplay: the predator has the gun.
annotation.definitionFit: Army ants hunt in huge swarming columns, predators of insects and small animals.

entries.clue: What's used in court to suppress fraud? (6,6)

blocks.note: a court for a ball game, where players swing something

annotation.surface: A question about what the law courts use to stamp out fraud.
annotation.walkthrough: The court is a sports court, not a law court.
annotation.definitionFit: A squash racket is what players swing on a squash court.
